newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch share bandwagon rolls to fresh closing high.
newsitem.headline: Dutch share bandwagon rolls to fresh closing high.

text.p: Dutch shares climbed to their fifth consecutive closing high on Monday -- the sixth closing record since the year began -- boosted by Friday's 68 point surge on Wall Street and continuing dollar strength.
The AEX share index closed 3.55 points up at a record 673.63, down from an all-time high of 675.62, which beat Friday's trading high of 673.36.

Some believe the market can go higher still as investors scramble to join a rally which has seen the AEX probe higher from 648 at the end of last year. Others, however, see a crack in sentiment on inflation worries tied to the dollar's strength.

Some said a new bullish dynamic appeared to be building up in equities with the AEX seen rising to yet more peaks this week, confounding some peoples' forecasts that the market might be set for a period of consolidation in the New Year.
They said trading on Monday was a lot quieter than on Friday. "I think we're seeing a few players picking up things that have been seen as underperforming," one said.

"Everyone's bullish right now," said another dealer. "With this level of interest it's easy to see the index around 680 to 690 this week although I think we'd get a pretty quick 20 point correction if the index went through 700," he added.
Analysts late last year had seen the index finishing 1997 with a modest rise to around 680, way behind the 30 percent plus rise notched up during the course of last year.
Dealers said low interest rates and the firm dollar were making Dutch equities more and more attractive. "Everbody in Holland wants to get involved in this market," a dealer said.

But some in the market believe a correction could come soon as the AEX heads into uncharted territory against the background of a rampant dollar. "A weaker guilder is fine for the exporters but it has inflationary implications for the Netherlands generally as imports get more expensive," a trader said.
